A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboStream and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Moved and renumbered material can be matched reliably, supporting comparison of the complete documents.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-world manipulation results, spatial-reasoning evaluations, component ablations, failure analysis, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds memory-baseline comparisons and runtime measurements across backbone and hardware configurations.

M1.justification: The RGB-D perception pipeline, STF-Tokens, CSTG updates, VLM planning, and deterministic action instantiation remain unchanged in Section 3. Token definitions and PointSO integration are retained; the added efficient-inference discussion does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same real-world tasks, SIMPLER embodiments, RLBench short- and long-horizon tasks, SpatialBench, and Open6DOR V2. The new memory-baseline comparison reuses four existing RLBench tasks, and the added runtime study uses the existing real-world suite.

E2.justification: New Appendix C.6 and Table 12 add SAM2Act and MemoryVLA as evaluated comparators on four retained RLBench tasks. Earlier comparator sets remain intact. Figure 1 changes its label from SoFar to Existing Methods while retaining the SoFar citation and corresponding example; this does not establish additional evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The added runtime experiment averages per-step latency across all real-world cases using 1, 2, and 8 A100 GPUs for the 8B, 32B, and 235B backbones. The original single-case timing experiment remains. Table 6 also relabels one disassembly case from Hard to Medium, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 extends runtime analysis from the retained seven-step 8B case to module-level timing across three backbone/hardware configurations and the real-world suite. This adds evidence about computational scaling. Existing component ablations, failure distributions, and qualitative task analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three executions per real-world task and 25 episodes with different random seeds for long-horizon RLBench evaluation. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-reporting procedure. The new latency averages do not establish additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 6 changes one hard-building result from 0/3 to 1/3 for SoFar and from 0/3 to 2/3 for RoboStream-8B; their building averages become 22.2% and 33.3%, previously 18.5% and 25.9%. The 32B average is corrected from 48.2% to 48.1%. New Table 12 reports SAM2Act/MemoryVLA averages of 30.0%/26.0%; Table 10 adds total latencies of 3.86, 8.61, and 5.15 seconds. These timings use different conditions from the retained Table 9, so they do not establish a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the definitions of geometric descriptors, spatial relations, STF-Tokens, and CSTG memory remain unchanged. Neither version introduces a theorem or proof that is added, removed, or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free geometric grounding through STF-Tokens and persistent causal memory through CSTG. The abstract retains the 90.5% RLBench and 44.4% hard block-building results, and the introduction retains the five-benchmark performance claim. The shortened conclusion preserves the same scientific message.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 explicitly distinguishes single-case and suite-wide timing, cautions against directly comparing their absolute latencies, and offers an MoE/hardware explanation for the 235B versus 32B runtime. Appendix B.2 softens proving absolute necessity into providing strong evidence for CSTG. The substantive limitations discussion is retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents GPU counts for the added cross-backbone timing study, its averaging scope, and approximately 22B active parameters for the 235B MoE backbone. It clarifies the retained single-case profiling scope. Robot setups, system prompts, existing sliding-window information, and the project website remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight cited works are added, covering SAM2Act, MemoryVLA, two works on 4D understanding, and four efficient-inference approaches. Section 3.3 newly positions compact STF-Tokens as orthogonal to inference acceleration. These are bounded additions; the main related-work organization and earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the conclusion, places limitations before it, expands the runtime explanation, and incorporates former Appendix D experiments into Appendix C. It also adds acknowledgments, edits author/affiliation information, and corrects wording and typos. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the runtime and memory-baseline tables, revises the retained latency-table caption, and relocates Figure 1 while generalizing its comparator label. Table styling, hyperlink colors, and some figure annotations change. Existing figures and experimental displays are otherwise retained, including the unchanged Figure 4.

improvement.justification: The added memory-baseline comparison makes the evidence more relevant to the central memory claim, while the expanded timing analysis clarifies deployment costs and comparison limits. Table 6 revisions resolve discrepancies with the retained Figure 4 for hard-building results. These provide a modest net improvement. Sparse configuration details for the new baselines and Figure 1's less specific comparator attribution limit the gain; the method and principal conclusions remain unchanged.
